best_idea: Keep one snapshot state per client with three send rates (INIT, FULL, RECOVER), diff each snapshot against the last tick the client acknowledged, and test interest per entity before writing it, so a far or hidden entity is simply absent and the delta reports it as removed.
decision_why: The rate state machine, delta-from-acked-base and per-entity interest test fit a phone client and the rule that the server owns what each viewer gets; reject the even-tick parity coupling and the silent item drop (both fixed in the sketch) and the spectator free-view clamp because the camera stays client-only; kills and hits stay on the reliable event path.
acceptance: A server test asserts a viewer that never acked gets a snapshot every 10 ticks (200 ms), every 2 ticks after its first ack, once per second when its base is lost, and that an entity 1001 units to the side of its view is absent from its snapshot and reported as removed.
